runs.summary: The review assessed the shareholders' agreement against the DMCC company-status, registration, Articles, licensing, Branch, name, continuation, and corporate-capacity provisions. The Company's separate legal personality, limited shareholder liability, and core licensing obligation are addressed. The principal issue is an incomplete licensing clause that omits statutory liability attribution and the twenty-four-week strike-off and dissolution consequences. The review identified direct conflicts concerning unapproved share denominations, bearer shares, capital reduction procedure and share transfers. It also identified deficient director qualification and alternate-director provisions, plus a missing director-change notification obligation. Dividend provisions were compliant on the stated terms, while holding-company and subsidiary rules were not applicable to the structure described. The review identified direct conflicts with mandatory DMCC requirements, including prohibited Director financial assistance, removal of the Company Secretary, non-compliant meeting rules, US GAAP accounting, an excessive first financial year and inadequate audit provisions. Manager, Officer disqualification, inspection and filing procedures are also incomplete or unclear. These issues should be aligned with the DMCCA Regulations and Officer Rules before reliance on the Agreement. The review assessed the agreement's winding-up, liquidation and DMCC licensing provisions against the listed DMCCA requirements. The agreement includes a solvency-declaration reference, liquidation payment priorities, liquidator qualification and licence-suspension language, but omits substantial mandatory reporting, creditor, liquidation, dissolution and strike-off requirements. Amalgamation, sanctions and unfair-prejudice provisions were treated as not applicable because they are not operative contractual subjects addressed by this agreement. The review assessed the Agreement against DMCCA disclosure obligations and voluntary licence suspension requirements. The disclosure clause is materially incomplete because it omits several mandatory reporting, information integrity, protection, and compliance requirements. The licence suspension wording addresses cessation generally but does not clearly reflect the prescribed voluntary suspension approval and Registrar process.

findings.title: Incomplete licence consequences
findings.description: The licensing provisions require a valid Licence and address suspension operationally, but do not state that liabilities or commitments incurred before the first Licence or during suspension are treated as liabilities or commitments of the Shareholders. They also omit the twenty-four-week deadline after registration and the Registrar's potential strike-off and automatic dissolution consequences.

findings.title: Unapproved Share Denominations
findings.description: Clause 1.5 allows additional shares to be issued in currencies or cryptocurrency-denominated tokens without DMCC Registrar approval. Shares must be denominated in UAE Dirhams or another currency approved by the Registrar.

findings.title: Invalid Capital Reduction
findings.description: Clause 8.1 makes a capital reduction effective immediately after the Special Resolution and excludes the required notice, publication and director solvency certificate.

findings.title: Bearer Shares Prohibited
findings.description: Clause 1.4 requires the Company to issue bearer share certificates and permits transfer by delivery without registration or Registrar notification.

findings.title: Incomplete Transfer Execution
findings.description: Clause 7.2 requires only the transferor's signature and delivery to the Registrar. DMCC registration requires a transfer document signed by or on behalf of both transferor and transferee and delivered to both the Registrar and the Company.

findings.title: Deficient Director Qualifications
findings.description: Clause 2.2 permits directors aged 16 or older and applies only a five-year dishonesty period, whereas the required thresholds are at least 18 and ten years. It also allows non-natural persons based only on shareholder agreement rather than the required Registrar approval.

findings.title: Unqualified Alternate Directors
findings.description: Clause 2.6 expressly permits an alternate director who does not meet the Agreement's qualification requirements, contrary to the requirement that every alternate meet the applicable qualification criteria.

findings.title: Missing Director Notifications
findings.description: The Agreement does not require changes to directors to be notified to the Registrar within fourteen Business Days.

findings.title: Prohibited Director Assistance
findings.description: Clause 2.5 permits loans, guarantees and other financial assistance to Directors, subject only to a monetary limit and shareholder approval. The regulatory prohibition is absolute and is not displaced by approval or amount.

findings.title: Incomplete Continuing Duties
findings.description: The Agreement refers only to confidential information and opportunities obtained during tenure. It does not preserve duties concerning exploitation of Company property or information generally, or acts and omissions occurring before cessation.

findings.title: Secretary Requirement Removed
findings.description: The Agreement states that the Company does not need a Secretary and assigns filing duties to other persons. A DMCC Company must have a Secretary, who must be appointed by Director resolution and perform the prescribed filing and officer duties.

findings.title: Manager Processes Incomplete
findings.description: The Agreement requires a Manager and a ten-Business-Day replacement but does not require appointment by Director resolution or notification to the Registrar within five Business Days after resignation, removal, death or incapacity.

findings.title: Disqualification Removal Missing
findings.description: The Agreement does not require Shareholders to remove a disqualified Director, or Directors to remove a disqualified Secretary or Manager, within ten Business Days of a disqualification order.

findings.title: Non-Compliant Meeting Rules
findings.description: The Agreement delays the first AGM and subsequent AGMs beyond the permitted periods, uses eight rather than ten Business Days' notice, permits a 50% quorum rather than more than 50%, and permits 75% written resolutions rather than unanimous written resolutions.

findings.title: Meeting Notice Content Incomplete
findings.description: Meeting notices state the basic logistics and business nature but omit the required statement of any proposed Ordinary or Special Resolution, its contents, and relevant accounts and auditor reports.

findings.title: Accounting Requirements Conflict
findings.description: The Agreement requires US GAAP rather than IFRS, allows a 24-month first financial year although the maximum is 18 months, and requires retention for only three years rather than at least five years.

findings.title: Accounts Procedures Incomplete
findings.description: The accounts provisions do not require Director approval and signature, examination and reporting within six months after year-end, presentation at a General Meeting, or filing with the Registrar within five Business Days after that meeting.

findings.title: Audit Requirements Incomplete
findings.description: The Agreement does not require appointment at a General Meeting, written auditor consent, confirmation that no disqualifying matter is known, or the full statutory auditor report. It also omits auditor access and prohibitions on misleading or withholding information.

findings.title: Inspection Cooperation Unclear
findings.description: The Agreement contains no provision addressing DMCCA inspection powers, production of records, attendance and assistance obligations, or compliance with Registrar directions and remedial deadlines.

findings.title: Missing distress reporting duties
findings.description: Section 11 does not require Directors to report to the Registrar within ten Business Days when the Company's purpose has expired, liabilities exceed assets, or employees remain unpaid for three consecutive months. It also omits the obligation to notify Shareholders within twenty-one days when losses reach 75% or more of Share Capital.

findings.title: Incomplete solvent winding-up process
findings.description: Clause 11.1 only states that Directors must make a declaration of solvency within twenty Business Days before the resolution. It does not state the declaration's required solvency alternatives, require Registrar submission of the declaration, appointment notice and minutes, or include liquidator reporting and final meeting procedures.

findings.title: Missing insolvent winding-up rules
findings.description: The agreement contains no procedures for an insolvent voluntary winding-up, including the creditor meeting timetable and notices, appointment of a chairman and liquidator, statement of affairs, creditor voting, Liquidation Committee or annual creditor meetings. It also omits the requirement that documents issued during winding-up state that the Company is in liquidation.

findings.title: Incomplete liquidation mechanics
findings.description: Clause 11.2 states the payment priority, but the agreement does not address the liquidator's statutory powers, duties of Officers and employees to assist, pari passu realisation of assets, distribution of any surplus to Shareholders, Registrar confirmation of dissolution or disposal and retention of records.

findings.title: Termination and strike-off omitted
findings.description: Section 9.2 addresses suspension by requiring the Company to cease operations other than meeting creditor obligations. It does not address the Company's immediate obligations following a Termination Notice, the strike-off notice process, continuing liability of Officers and Shareholders, personal liability for purported obligations or the requirement to commence winding-up after strike-off.

findings.title: Incomplete disclosure obligations
findings.description: Clause 12.1 does not cover all matters required by the Regulations, including likely failures to comply, other prescribed matters attributable to officers or representatives, prohibitions on false or misleading information and concealment, protection from detriment, and compliance with Registrar directions or requirements.

findings.title: Suspension process is incomplete
findings.description: Clause 9.2 only addresses the consequences of a suspended licence. It does not incorporate the Ordinary Resolution requirement, Registrar approval or request process, maximum suspension period, or rules governing dormant or voluntarily suspended companies.

runs.summary: The review considered whether the shareholders' agreement reflects the DMCC requirements applicable to company status, licensing and corporate capacity. The document appropriately states separate legal personality, limited Shareholder liability and licence-based operating restrictions. A material omission remains concerning the statutory treatment of liabilities and commitments incurred before licensing or while the Licence is suspended. The review identified direct conflicts concerning bearer shares, share currencies, capital reductions, share transfers and Director requirements. Several provisions also leave class-rights, Treasury Share and cryptocurrency-distribution safeguards unclear or incomplete. The Articles and actual DMCC register and filing arrangements should be checked against the Agreement before implementation. The review identified material conflicts with DMCC requirements covering Directors, the Secretary, the Manager, General Meetings, accounts and audit. The most significant issues are the express authorization of prohibited financial assistance to Directors, the denial of a mandatory Secretary, incorrect meeting and financial-year periods, US GAAP instead of IFRS, and incomplete audit controls. The agreement should be revised to preserve the statutory requirements and deadlines, with the Articles and DMCC filings checked separately. The review identified material omissions concerning amalgamation, pre-insolvency reporting and the full solvent, summary and insolvent winding-up regimes. The Agreement also incompletely addresses licence termination and strike-off consequences, liquidation administration, and statutory contravention and unfair-prejudice exposure. Sanctions and administrative fines were treated as not applicable to the drafting of this shareholders' agreement. The review examined the Agreement’s disclosure and licence-suspension provisions against C33 and C34. Clause 12.1 is materially incomplete because it does not capture the full range of disclosure duties and safeguards. Clause 9.2 addresses suspension generally but leaves the statutory voluntary-suspension process and conditions unclear.

findings.title: Licence liability allocation missing
findings.description: Section 9 requires the Company to maintain a Licence and cease operations on suspension, but it does not state that liabilities or commitments entered into before the first Licence or during suspension are treated as liabilities or commitments of the Shareholders.

findings.title: Unauthorised Share Currencies
findings.description: The Agreement permits additional shares to be denominated in currencies or cryptocurrency tokens selected by the Board without DMCC Registrar approval. Shares must be denominated in AED or another currency approved by the Registrar.

findings.title: Defective Capital Reduction
findings.description: The Agreement states that a capital reduction takes effect immediately after the Special Resolution and expressly excludes publication, Registrar notice and a Director solvency certificate. These statutory steps cannot be disapplied by the Agreement.

findings.title: Bearer Shares Prohibited
findings.description: The Agreement requires bearer share certificates and purports to allow transfer by physical delivery without registration or Registrar notification. DMCC companies may not issue bearer shares.

findings.title: Missing Class Rights Controls
findings.description: The Agreement refers to the Articles but does not state the procedure for varying class rights or the restrictions and treatment applicable to Treasury Shares. The Articles must be checked and aligned with the Regulations.

findings.title: Incomplete Transfer Execution
findings.description: The transfer procedure requires only the transferor's signature and delivery to the Registrar. DMCC registration requires a transfer document signed by or for both transferor and transferee and delivered to both the Registrar and the Company.

findings.title: Uncontrolled Crypto Dividends
findings.description: The Agreement permits cryptocurrency dividends based on a Board-determined conversion rate but does not require the distribution to be valued at the statutory value or address the Company's entitlement to receive that value for a non-cash distribution.

findings.title: Unqualified Alternate Directors
findings.description: The Agreement expressly states that an alternate Director need not meet the Director qualification requirements, contrary to the requirement that an alternate satisfy the applicable qualification criteria.

findings.title: Missing Director Notifications
findings.description: The Agreement requires notification of Manager or Secretary changes but does not require notification of changes to Directors within 14 Business Days.

findings.title: Prohibited Director Assistance
findings.description: The agreement permits loans, guarantees and other financial assistance to Directors, subject only to monetary and shareholder-approval limits. DMCCA prohibits a Company from providing financial assistance to a Director.

findings.title: Incomplete Continuing Duties
findings.description: The agreement covers confidential information and opportunities but omits property and acts or omissions occurring before cessation, both of which remain subject to statutory duties.

findings.title: Secretary Requirement Disclaimed
findings.description: The Company is stated not to require a Secretary. Unless the Company is an SPV, DMCCA requires every Company to have a Secretary appointed by Director resolution.

findings.title: Manager Rules Incomplete
findings.description: The agreement does not require appointment of the Manager by Director resolution, does not state all statutory qualification restrictions, and does not include the five-Business-Day notification deadline after resignation, removal, death or incapacity.

findings.title: Interim Manager Mechanism Missing
findings.description: The agreement says Directors shall assume responsibilities if the Manager leaves office, but does not state that this occurs automatically or cover death and incapacity expressly.

findings.title: Officer Compliance Framework Missing
findings.description: The agreement does not allocate responsibility for procuring statutory filings or require timely removal of a Director, Secretary or Manager following a DMCCA disqualification order.

findings.title: AGM Schedule Too Long
findings.description: The agreement permits the first AGM within 36 months and subsequent AGMs every 18 months, whereas DMCCA requires the first AGM within 18 months and thereafter every 12 months unless the Articles provide a shorter period.

findings.title: Meeting Notice Too Short
findings.description: The agreement provides eight Business Days' notice for any General Meeting. DMCCA requires ten Business Days unless shorter notice is agreed by Shareholders holding at least 95% of total voting rights.

findings.title: Quorum Below Requirement
findings.description: The agreement sets the quorum at not less than 50%, while the default DMCCA quorum is more than 50% of total voting rights unless the Articles provide otherwise.

findings.title: Written Resolution Threshold Wrong
findings.description: The agreement allows written resolutions signed by holders of 75% of voting rights. DMCCA gives written resolutions the effect of meeting resolutions only when signed by all Shareholders entitled to vote.

findings.title: Meeting Administration Omissions
findings.description: The notice provision does not require the intention and contents of proposed Ordinary or Special Resolutions or relevant accounts and auditor reports. The agreement also omits the 10% EGM requisition process and Minutes Register requirements.

findings.title: Incorrect Accounting Standard
findings.description: The agreement requires accounts to be prepared under US GAAP. DMCCA requires accounts to be prepared in accordance with IFRS.

findings.title: First Financial Year Too Long
findings.description: The agreement sets the first financial year at 24 months. DMCCA requires the first financial year to be at least six months and no longer than 18 months.

findings.title: Financial Reporting Process Missing
findings.description: The agreement does not require accounts to be approved by Directors, examined by a DMCCA-approved auditor and laid before a General Meeting within six months after year-end, followed by filing within five Business Days.

findings.title: Retention Period Too Short
findings.description: The agreement requires retention for three years, while DMCCA requires accounting records to be preserved for at least five years, or 15 years for real-estate records.

findings.title: Auditor Appointment Incomplete
findings.description: The agreement requires an approved auditor but does not require appointment at a General Meeting, written consent, or confirmation that no known matter precludes consent.

findings.title: Auditor Report Incomplete
findings.description: The auditor report provision omits whether the accounts were properly prepared in accordance with IFRS and whether they give a true and fair view of the Company's affairs, and it does not include other DMCCA-required matters.

findings.title: Auditor Safeguards Missing
findings.description: There are no provisions addressing auditor access to records, requests for information and explanations, investigation duties, or prohibitions on misleading, coercing or withholding information from the auditor.

findings.title: Auditor Cessation Rules Missing
findings.description: The agreement does not require a departing auditor to deposit a statement concerning matters requiring shareholder or creditor attention and does not address a 10% shareholder's right to require an audit of a dormant Company.

findings.title: Amalgamation framework missing
findings.description: There is no process for amalgamation with another DMCC Company or a Non-DMCC Entity, including Registrar consent, shareholder resolutions, authorisations and solvency or creditor-protection declarations.

findings.title: Pre-insolvency duties omitted
findings.description: The Agreement does not require Directors to report specified financial distress or unpaid employee conditions to the Registrar within ten Business Days, or require notification to Shareholders when losses reach 75% of share capital.

findings.title: Solvent winding-up incomplete
findings.description: The Agreement requires a solvency declaration but does not require the prescribed declaration content, liquidator appointment by General Meeting, or submission of the appointment notice, declaration and minutes to the Registrar.

findings.title: Insolvent procedures omitted
findings.description: No provisions address the required Creditors' meeting, notice periods, chairman, proposed liquidator, signed statement of affairs, creditor appointment of the liquidator, liquidation committee or annual creditor meetings.

findings.title: Liquidation powers incomplete
findings.description: The Agreement states the payment priority but omits the liquidator's statutory powers, pari passu application of property, distribution of surplus to Shareholders, cooperation obligations and Registrar confirmation of dissolution.

findings.title: Strike-off consequences omitted
findings.description: The Agreement covers licence suspension but does not state the DMCCA termination grounds or the notice, response, public-notice and post-strike-off winding-up process.

findings.title: Contravention remedies incomplete
findings.description: The disclosure clause does not address that persons knowingly concerned in a contravention may themselves commit a contravention, nor does the Agreement address statutory Court remedies for unfairly prejudicial conduct.

findings.title: Incomplete disclosure obligations
findings.description: Clause 12.1 requires disclosure of matters indicating a contravention, but does not expressly cover likely failures to comply with obligations, other matters prescribed by DMCCA, auditor disclosure duties, false or misleading information, concealment, compliance with Registrar directions, or protection from detriment for good-faith reporting.

findings.title: Unclear voluntary suspension process
findings.description: The Agreement requires cessation of operations when a licence is suspended, but does not state the Ordinary Resolution requirement, Registrar or DMCC rules, permitted suspension period, or that trading remains prohibited until formal reactivation.

runs.summary: The review assessed the shareholders' agreement against the DMCC company, registration, Articles, licensing, Branch, naming, continuation, and corporate-capacity requirements. The document adequately states the Company's separate personality, limited shareholder liability, and general Licence obligations. A high-risk gap remains in Section 9 because it does not address all mandatory licensing conditions and consequences under C4. The review identified direct conflicts concerning bearer shares, share issuance currencies, capital reduction procedures and share-transfer formalities. Director eligibility and alternate-director provisions also fall short of the DMCC requirements, while the dividend approval threshold is unclear. Other reviewed provisions were either compliant on their face or not applicable based on the document's stated structure. The review identified direct conflicts with DMCC requirements on Director financial assistance, the Company Secretary, Manager procedures, meetings, accounts and audit. The most significant issues are the authorization of prohibited financial assistance, elimination of the Secretary, non-compliant meeting and accounting periods, and use of US GAAP instead of IFRS. DMCCA inspection and Registrar-direction powers were treated as not applicable to the required contractual terms. The review identified omissions across all eight listed DMCCA regulatory areas. The Agreement partially addresses voluntary winding-up, liquidation payment priority, liquidator qualifications, and licence suspension, but does not capture the broader statutory procedures, reporting duties, enforcement consequences, amalgamation requirements, or unfair-prejudice remedies. Several omissions create high risk because they concern mandatory deadlines, creditor protections, insolvency procedures, and Registrar or DMCCA actions. The review checked the agreement’s disclosure provisions and licence-suspension terms against C33 and C34. C33 is violated because Section 12 is incomplete and omits several required regulatory safeguards. C34 is addressed consistently by the requirement to cease operations during licence suspension.

findings.title: Incomplete licensing regime
findings.description: Section 9 addresses maintaining a Licence and conducting only licensed activities, but does not reflect the full requirements that operations require both a Certificate of Registration and a Licence. It also omits the statutory treatment of liabilities and commitments incurred before the first Licence or during Licence suspension, and the Registrar's ability to strike off and dissolve a Company that has not obtained a Licence within twenty-four weeks of registration.

findings.title: Incomplete transfer procedure

findings.title: Solvency approval threshold unclear
findings.description: The dividend provision requires a Directors' solvency resolution but does not specify the simple-majority threshold required by the Regulations.

findings.title: Non-compliant director qualifications
findings.description: The agreement permits directors aged 16 or 17 and uses a five-year dishonesty lookback, while DMCC requires directors to be at least 18 and applies a ten-year period. It also omits disqualification and suitability requirements.

findings.title: Unqualified alternate directors
findings.description: The alternate-director provision conflicts with the requirement that an alternate meet the applicable director qualification criteria.

findings.title: Registrar notification missing
findings.description: The agreement does not require the Company to notify the Registrar of appointments, resignations, removals or other changes to Directors within fourteen Business Days.

findings.title: Prohibited Financial Assistance
findings.description: Clause 2.5 authorizes loans, guarantees and other financial assistance to Directors, subject only to monetary and shareholder-approval limits. The regulatory prohibition is absolute and is not displaced by shareholder approval.

findings.title: Incomplete Continuing Duties
findings.description: The Agreement continues only duties regarding confidential information and opportunities, but does not preserve duties concerning all property, information or opportunities and things done or omitted before cessation.

findings.title: Secretary Requirement Removed
findings.description: The Agreement states that the Company does not need a Secretary. A DMCC Company must have a Secretary, subject to the SPV exception, which the document does not invoke.

findings.title: Manager Procedures Incomplete
findings.description: The Manager section requires a natural-person Manager but does not provide for appointment by Director resolution. It also uses a fourteen-Business-Day notification period for all changes and omits the separate five-Business-Day notification requirement after resignation, removal, death or incapacity.

findings.title: Director Disqualification Conflict
findings.description: The Agreement permits Directors aged sixteen or older and uses a five-year dishonesty-conviction period, while the regulatory criteria require at least eighteen and ten years. It also permits an alternate Director to bypass the stated qualifications.

findings.title: Non-Compliant Meeting Rules
findings.description: The Agreement delays the first AGM to thirty-six months and later AGMs to eighteen-month intervals, permits eight-Business-Day notice, uses a 50% quorum, and permits 75% written resolutions. These terms conflict with the required statutory periods, notice, quorum and unanimous written-resolution rule.

findings.title: Non-Compliant Accounting Framework
findings.description: The Agreement mandates US GAAP rather than IFRS, creates a twenty-four-month first financial year exceeding the eighteen-month maximum, and requires retention for only three years rather than at least five years.

findings.title: Excessive First Financial Year
findings.description: The first financial year is stated to end twenty-four months after registration, whereas the permitted maximum is eighteen months.

findings.title: Insufficient Record Retention
findings.description: The Agreement requires preservation of accounting records for only three years, omitting the five-year minimum required for ordinary records.

findings.title: Incomplete Audit Requirements
findings.description: The Agreement requires an approved auditor but does not require appointment at a General Meeting, written consent, confirmation of no disqualifying matter, or the full statutory auditor-report contents and investigation rights.

findings.title: Amalgamation requirements omitted
findings.description: The Agreement does not address amalgamation of DMCC Companies or amalgamation involving Non-DMCC Entities. It therefore omits the required Registrar consent and supporting resolutions, authorisations, solvency, asset-value, and creditor-protection documentation where applicable.

findings.title: Pre-insolvency duties missing
findings.description: The Agreement does not require Directors to report expired purpose, cessation of business, excess liabilities, or unpaid employees to the Registrar within ten Business Days. It also omits the 75% share-capital-loss notification requirement and the statutory winding-up framework.

findings.title: Solvent winding-up incomplete
findings.description: Section 11.1 mentions a solvency declaration but does not require the declaration to contain the prescribed statements, nor does it address liquidator appointment, Registrar submissions, cessation of Director powers, annual progress reports, final meetings, or final filings.

findings.title: Insolvent procedures omitted
findings.description: The Agreement does not address the creditor meeting timetable and notices, chairman, statement of affairs, creditor appointment of the liquidator, liquidation committee, annual creditor meetings, or the requirement that winding-up documents state that the Company is in liquidation.

findings.title: Liquidation completion rules missing
findings.description: Section 11.2 does not state that property is realised and applied pari passu after the specified priority, or how surplus property and records are handled. The Agreement also omits liquidator powers, official cooperation duties, and dissolution upon Registrar confirmation.

findings.title: DMCCA sanctions unaddressed
findings.description: The Agreement does not acknowledge that DMCCA may impose service restrictions, fines, licence suspension or termination, strike-off, and other sanctions for contraventions, or prescribe fines and recovery procedures.

findings.title: Strike-off consequences missing
findings.description: Section 9.2 correctly addresses cessation during licence suspension, but the Agreement omits licence termination grounds, termination notices, strike-off notices and public notice, continuing Officer and Shareholder liability, and the obligation to commence winding-up after strike-off.

findings.title: Contraventions and prejudice omitted
findings.description: The Agreement does not address liability for knowingly participating in a contravention, including aiding, procuring, concealing, or obstructing investigation. It also omits the Court’s remedies for affairs conducted in a manner unfairly prejudicial to shareholders.

findings.title: Incomplete disclosure safeguards
findings.description: Clause 12 covers contraventions and internal systems, but does not expressly cover likely failures to comply with obligations or other prescribed matters. It also omits the prohibitions on false, misleading or deceptive information and concealment, compliance with Registrar directions, and protection against detriment for good-faith reporting.
